prize_parts.citation: For the development of general palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: Pd-catalysed C-N coupling is a general, ligand-controlled reaction whose scope, mechanism and industrial uptake are not in doubt, and it has been independently confirmed for more than two decades. The attribution is the cleanest among the strong candidates: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the ligand-enabled catalytic amination, giving a natural two-person prize with no forced exclusions. It is a synthetic-methodology achievement of the kind the chemistry prize has honoured repeatedly, and the 2010 prize covered C-C coupling rather than this chapter. After reading colleagues' ballots I keep it first because it is the only top candidate for which both the discovery and the credit are settled.
statement.case_against: The 2010 cross-coupling prize may make a closely related reaction look incremental, and the scientific question here is more a matter of generalisation than of a new concept. Kosugi's earlier aminostannane coupling is a genuine precursor whose treatment in a citation has to be handled carefully. Targeted protein degradation (B023) is conceptually fresher and has much stronger opening support, and I may be underweighting the novelty of a new drug modality relative to a mature synthetic method.

responses.point: Induced proximity through bifunctional degraders and molecular glues is a clean chemical idea that opens undruggable targets and is moving into the clinic, which is why B023 deserves first place.
responses.response: I accept the conceptual originality and the mechanistic clarity, and I moved B023 up in my own thinking after reading the ballots. My reservation is attribution and maturity. PROTACs and molecular glues are arguably two discoveries, and your three-person cut of Crews, Deshaies and Handa leaves out Ciulli, Gray and Ito, whose contributions are comparable. An approved degrader has also not yet validated the modality. These issues are not disqualifying, but they are why I keep B002, where neither problem arises, ahead of it.

responses.point: Buchwald-Hartwig amination is the defining methodology advance for aryl amines, fully mature and overdue, and Kosugi's tin-based precursor was not general, so a two-person prize is the cleaner configuration.
responses.response: I agree with the two-person configuration and with the view that Kosugi was a precursor and not the originator of the general reaction. I would still ask the committee to take your own caveat seriously: precedence should be handled in the citation wording, and the case for Kosugi cannot simply be dismissed. I also share your sense that the 2010 prize did not cover this chapter, but I recognise that others find the overlap decisive, so I would not claim the case is free of risk.

responses.point: B002 is clear, original and of lasting practical impact but sits in the shadow of the 2010 prize, while B023 brings structural, physical-organic and medicinal chemistry together at the molecular level.
responses.response: I think the 2010 shadow is real, and it is the strongest argument against my own first choice. The two prizes honour different bond constructions with different ligand design and mechanistic problems, and C-N bonds are central to drug molecules. On B023, I agree that ternary-complex cooperativity and linker design give it rich molecular content, but I think the allocation problem you describe as unresolved is more serious than you suggest, because the discovery splits between PROTAC and cereblon lineages.

responses.point: Halide perovskites (B009) turned a simple solution-processable semiconductor into a photovoltaic absorber rivalling silicon in about a decade, though stability, toxicity and contested priority among six names complicate recognition.
responses.response: I rank B009 second as well, and the scientific impact is established. I do not see a three-person configuration that is defensible, though. Miyasaka, Park and Snaith leave out Kanatzidis, Seok and Grätzel, and I do not think the committee can resolve those priority questions with confidence. Unresolved long-term stability also makes it a weaker prize now than a mature synthetic method, so I keep it as an alternative and not as my preferred choice.

uncertainties: How much weight the committee gives the 2010 cross-coupling prize when judging whether C-N coupling is a distinct discovery.
Whether and how Kosugi's precursor work should be reflected in the citation.
Whether the PROTAC and molecular-glue lineages in B023 can be combined into one prize with a defensible three-person allocation.
My assessments rest on recalled knowledge and not on independent verification of priority claims.
statement.conflict_note: My profile records that Peter Brzezinski, the Secretary, is a Stockholm University colleague, and that I work in electron crystallography and porous materials; this bears on B032 and B054, which I did not propose, and none of the candidates in my preferred configuration is connected to my own research. No specific conflict requiring recusal is apparent from the provided profile for B002, B023 or B009.
